Local Project Coordinator - Équateur Province, DRC for Gender Outcomes in Jurisdictional REDD+ Program

Term: Full time, initial term 1 year
Location: Équateur Province, DRC (Work a min of 4 overlapping hours with the North America Central time zone)
Company Summary
Founded in 2006, Terra Global is a woman-founded, woman-run for-profit social enterprise, and small business. Terra Global's mission is to attract private sector capital to Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to produce significant climate change mitigation, community and biodiversity benefits. Terra Global is an industry leader in NbS program development, land-use greenhouse gas and impact quantification, and climate asset creation, with experience in 40 countries at project and jurisdictional scales. Terra Global is the only company with end-to-end knowledge of carbon development and climate finance transactions. We deliver proven expertise working on-the-ground with local partners, while leveraging financial and transaction structuring expertise to equitably balance risk and return between Investors and Investees. Project Background
The Integrating Gender Outcomes-Based Financing into a JREDD+ Program in Équateur Province, DRC grant is piloting an innovative model that integrates verified gender impact outcomes into a Jurisdictional REDD+ (JREDD+) Program in the Équateur Province, DRC and seeking to attract outcome-based finance that complements climate finance. While JREDD+ programs are effective at mobilizing climate finance to reduce deforestation, they do not explicitly measure or fund women’s contributions or activities that benefit women, despite women being central actors in forest conservation and community livelihoods. In the Équateur Province, forest-dependent communities manage extensive forest areas through Community Forest Concessions (CFCLs). Within these systems, women play a critical role in subsistence agriculture and fuelwood, and Non-Timber Forest Product (NTFP) collection. However, they face persistent structural barriers, including limited access to income-generating opportunities, restricted control over assets, exclusion from decision-making processes, and disproportionate unpaid labor burdens. These factors limit the effectiveness and durability of forest conservation efforts. Inclusive, equitable programs improve compliance, reduce conflict, and bolster environmental outcomes. Despite this, existing REDD+ financing channels often do not explicitly recognize the important role women play in forest conservation.
This pilot aims to address that gap by designing a Gender Based Outcome Finance Program embedded within a JREDD+ Program, using the W+ Standard[1] to define, measure, and verify outcomes across key domains related to women’s empowerment (access to income and assets, time savings, and leadership). The pilot will design a Gender Based Program that benefits approximately 4,556 women across 28 villages in five CFCLs, covering over 115,000 hectares of threatened forest area. This pilot will be co-designed with local partners and beneficiaries through participatory consultations, Theory of Change (TOC) workshops, and capacity building sessions.
Outcomes for the 12-month grant period include:

• Conduct community consultation with gender focus.

• Design Gender-focused activities through a participatory process.

• Define baseline for gender outcomes under the W+ Standard.

• Develop the Monitoring plan in accordance with the W+ Standard.

• Develop the W+ Project Description Document (PDD).

• Pilot the demand for Gender Based Outcome Finance.

Responsibilities
The Local Project Coordinator will provide technical support and coordination for the engagement with Concessions Forestières des Communautés Locales (Local Community Forest Concessions-CFCLs). This will be overseeing and supporting the implementation partners (CFCL operators) to design gender focused activities, collect field data and implement activities to meet W+ Standard requirement

description:
NVIDIA Networking product security team is looking for an outstanding technical security architect with hands-on experience to help us improve the security posture of NVIDIA networking products. In this role you will partner with firmware, hardware, and architecture teams on the security architecture, to reduce risk, threats, and vulnerabilities while driving new security features that affect millions of devices all over the world!

What you'll be doing:

• Be involved in the security architecture of NVIDIA Networking firmware - trust boundaries, privilege separation between firmware domains, device identity and key storage, secure boot and chain of trust, and secure update and anti-rollback flows.

• Perform security threat modeling of firmware and embedded subsystems across NVIDIA Networking products.

• Analyze complex firmware and hardware/firmware interactions to identify security weaknesses, including boot flows, privileged execution environments, and host- and network-facing management interfaces.

• Define security features and mitigations spanning the full device lifecycle - provisioning, attestation, debug authorization, runtime hardening, and field update. Guide the engineering teams throughout the implementation.

• Translate threat models into actionable security requirements and architectural decisions, and review designs and implementations against them.

• Partner with hardware and ASIC architects to specify the security primitives firmware depends on, and define how they are used across the product line.

• Drive secure development practices for firmware - memory-safe coding patterns in C, static analysis, and fuzzing of firmware-exposed interfaces - and make sure development processes meet security and coding standards.

What we need to see:

• Academic degree in computer science, electrical engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience).

• Demonstrated experience of 8+ years in product security, firmware security, or security research, including hands-on work with embedded or firmware codebases.

• Experience defining security policy models - authorization schemes, RBAC, and administrative role separation - including how policy is expressed, enforced, and administered in production.

• Familiarity with applied cryptography (including secure boot, code signing, and attestation), threat modeling, common attack vectors, and mitigation techniques.

• Ability to work independently, and collaboratively in a constantly evolving environment.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• M.Sc. or PhD in computer science, electrical engineering, or related technical field.

• Experience with hardware/software interfaces in networking devices - register and MMIO programming models, DMA, mailbox and doorbell mechanisms, PCIe configuration and management interfaces, and the firmware that drives them.

• Experience with hardware roots of trust and hardware-enforced isolation (MPU/MMU, secure enclaves, fuse/OTP-based provisioning) in SoCs or ASICs.

• Hands-on experience with networking software - device drivers, control plane, management interfaces, or embedded network operating systems - and an understanding of how these components interact with firmware.

• Familiarity with high-scale deployment, the data center security ecosystem and its operational challenges.

title: Senior Identity Governance Engineer
description:
Ready to be a Titan?
At ServiceTitan , we are building a next-generation identity fabric, and this role engineers the governance layer on top of it. Identity spans cloud environments, SaaS applications, data systems, machine identities, and now AI agents, which makes it one of the most sprawling attack surfaces in the enterprise. You will make sure every identity, whether a Titan, a third-party contractor, a service account, or an AI agent, has the right access, for the right reason, at the right time, and that we can prove it.

Corporate Engineering (IT) administer our identity platforms, including Okta and Lumos, and run lifecycle operations. InfoSec defines identity governance requirements and validates that controls work. You sit in InfoSec and engineer the governance layer: authentication and authorization design standards, entitlement models, access review automation, and audit-ready evidence. You administer Veza with Corporate Security, Security Architecture, Product Security, and Security Operations, work with Corporate Engineering and System Owners to put governance requirements into practice, and you will be a key owner of our ISPM and IGA program.

What you'll do:
You engineer identity governance: the tooling, automation, and design standards that make access reviewable and provable. Corporate Engineering and IT administer the identity platforms, and InfoSec GRC owns the policies and the review program.

•
Access Request Governance: Define governance requirements and design patterns for access request workflows across privileged systems (code repositories, databases, infrastructure), including role-based, time-bound, delegated, and just-in-time access, and measure adoption so access is not granted outside the governed workflow. Corporate Engineering and IT administer Lumos and implement the workflows; you specify the requirements, build the monitoring that detects bypass, and validate that they work.

•
Authentication & Authorization Design: Partner with Security Architecture to define authentication and authorization design standards (SSO, MFA and phishing-resistant requirements, OIDC/SAML/SCIM patterns, least-privilege role models) for enterprise tools, and review integrations against them.

•
Authorization Governance & Entitlement Design: Provide the technical design for authorization decisions on job functions and privileged data access, including critical systems such as ST Admin roles, Snowflake, Salesforce, and other high-risk entitlements. Build role models scoped to job function and normalize entitlement data across applications in Veza so access can be reviewed like for like.

•
Access Review & Lifecycle Automation: Build and operate the tooling and automation behind the user access review program (SOX ITGC, PCI DSS, SOC 1/2, ISO 27001), which InfoSec GRC owns, and behind joiner/mover/leaver control assurance, including leaver access-reversion evidence, reconciliation against the authoritative HR source, and orphaned account detection.

•
Privileged Access Governance: Build visibility into standing privileged access across core cloud infrastructure and the data platform and drive it down, moving toward time-bound elevation (PIM and JIT) with governed exceptions for the access that must remain.

•
Identity Fabric Architecture: Define the target-state governance architecture across Okta, Veza, and Lumos and the risk-based identity lifecycle it supports. You administer Veza in combination with Corporate Security, Security Architecture, Product Security, and Security Operations, building its data source integrations, policies, and alerts. Corporate Engineering and IT administer Okta and Lumos, and you partner with them on lifecycle and workflow integration.

•
ISPM & Continuous Governance: Add continuous monitoring to periodic certifications. Build identity analytics that detect over-privileged accounts, shadow identities, dormant access, and identity drift, and automate remediation workflows with named owners

We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

CONSTRUCTION SUPERINTENDENT, STRUCTURAL

Most construction jobs manage someone else’s crew on someone else’s schedule, then end when the project does. This one does not.

SpaceX builds its own launch sites, factories, test stands, and AI superclusters - and it plans to keep building. The rockets, the chips, and the missions only matter if the ground under them is real. Construction is how that ground gets built, in-house and to a standard the company can actually use. The work does not dry up between jobs. There is a next site, and one after that. You lead the crew that builds them.You own a self-performing team. Foremen run their people day to day. You run the foremen. You are in the dirt, walking the work, setting the bar, and clearing whatever is in the way. When someone is ready for more, you say so. When the standard slips, you deal with it.

Crane and rigging work is in scope when it is raising the structure. Welding is in scope when it is steel structure.
